subject: Private Connector: Controlled Exit IPs, DNS Routing, and Firewall Zoning
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@orchidhealth.com
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private connector — egress & firewall zoning questions

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving forward with a short pilot of Redwood Private in our staging VPC and need to align on a small but strict set of network controls before flipping it to prod. Two specific asks from our SecOps team:

1) Which IPs (ranges) do we need to permit outbound from our private connector instances so that control-plane telemetry and model variants continue to work? Do you provide static egress IPs we can allow, or do we need to NAT via our corporate egress IPs?

2) We have a split-horizon DNS setup and want to avoid leaking internal names to the public DNS. How should we configure DNS forwarding for Redwood probes and health checks?

Attached is our standard security questionnaire — mostly checkboxes. If you can point to the specific firewall policy and an example runbook for failover, that will help speed our procurement signoff.

Best,
Samira Khan
Director, Cloud Security
Orchid Health

Attachments: orchid-soc2-questions.pdf (88KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector — egress & firewall zoning questions

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then actionable items we can include in a runbook.

Summary answers:
- Static egress: For Private deployments we support two patterns: (A) Redwood-managed static egress blocks (a small set of regional /29–/24 blocks we publish and rotate on a schedule), or (B) customer-controlled egress (your NAT gateway / proxy). If you want the simplest firewall rule set, choose Redwood-managed static egress.
- DNS: We recommend split-horizon with conditional forwarding for redwood-internal.* hostnames to your internal resolver. For health checks we prefer: outbound DNS queries to your internal resolver (so internal names resolve) and egress to 8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1 only for reachability checks if explicitly allowed.
- Ports & protocols: Allow outbound TCP 443 to the egress blocks, and UDP/TCP 53 only to your internal DNS resolver(s). For metrics/alerts we use TLS and will present a Redwood certificate (TLS 1.3 preferred).
- Certificate validation & pinning: We sign control-plane certs with public CA; customers may additionally validate via issuer and SAN. We can support strict cert pinning on request, but it complicates rotation.

Actionable details (for your firewall/NAT team):
1) If using Redwood-managed egress: allow outbound TCP/443 to the following CIDR list (attached). We will coordinate a maintenance window when we rotate these addresses.
2) If using customer NAT: ensure SNAT preserves source port mapping for long-lived streams. Provide us with the public IP(s) used by your NAT so we can bind model session state and identify requests in logs.
3) DNS setup: create a conditional forwarder for *.private.redwood.local to your internal resolver (10.10.10.2 / 10.10.10.3). Configure iptables/route table so that DNS requests for public names still follow your normal egress.
4) Health checks & probes: allow outbound to metrics.redwood.ai and status.redwood.ai (TLS 443). We use SNI-based routing on these endpoints.

I'll attach the current egress list (CSV) and a one-page sample firewall rule set. Olga, could you add a short note about logging/IDS expectations?

Next steps:
- I'll schedule a 30-min runbook review with your SecOps for Friday.
- If you prefer customer NAT, send the list of public IPs we should bind to.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-egress-ip-blocks.csv (3KB), redwood-firewall-sample.txt (1KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector — egress & firewall zoning questions

Hi Samira — quick note from SecOps/Platform:

- Logging/IDS: We emit audit logs for control-plane calls, model loads, and token-level errors to a TLS endpoint. If you need these pushed into your SIEM, we can arrange a secure delivery (syslog over TLS or HTTPS pull).
- Fallback & routing: Recommend adding allow rules for our regional fallback ranges (included in the CSV under column "fallback_range"). That keeps customer apps available during partial regional outages.
- KMS and keywrap: If you use our managed KMS integrations, ensure outbound to kms.redwood.ai and key-mgmt.redwood.ai (443) is permitted. If you require customer-side HSM connectivity, we can walk through direct peering.

I'll join the runbook call and bring an example IDS suppression list so your team can avoid noisy false positives on long-lived model streams.

—Olga
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector — egress & firewall zoning questions

Thanks — a few follow-ups from our engineering lead:

- DNS: Would you accept TLS-over-HTTPS (DoH) to an internal resolver, or do you strictly require UDP/TCP 53? We prefer DoH for telemetry flows to keep visibility on DNS queries.
- Certificate pinning: Our risk team prefers pinning to the issuing CA + SAN checks. Can Redwood provide key rotation windows and an expected notification lead time?
- SOC2 items: we attached the questionnaire. Please indicate which items are covered by your managed pattern vs. which require customer controls.

Also, our procurement needs a vendor-maintained runbook that includes an on-call escalation path and a pre-approved maintenance window. Can you share a short runbook template?

Regards,
Samira

Attachments: orchid-soc2-questions.pdf (88KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector — egress & firewall zoning questions

Great questions — answers below and a proposed schedule:

DoH vs native DNS: We support both. For private deployments we prefer native DNS to internal resolvers for name resolution of internal hostnames, but we can accept DoH for outgoing telemetry/telemetry-relay if your resolver supports an internal DoH endpoint. We'll need a short test plan to validate timing and connection reuse.

Certificate rotation & notifications: We rotate control-plane certs quarterly. For customers that enable strict pinning, we provide a 21-day advance notification and a canary endpoint to validate the new certs. We'll document the exact thumbprints in the runbook we share.

SOC2 questionnaire: We've annotated your PDF and marked answers that are covered by Redwood-managed deployments vs. customer responsibilities. See the attached "orchid-soc2-questions.pdf" (reviewed). For anything marked as "customer control", we'll call that out in the runbook checklist.

Runbook & on-call: I'll attach a one-page runbook template in the follow-up. Proposed runbook review meeting: Monday 2026-10-12 10:00 PT (30 min). Please confirm.

Action items for Orchid Health:
- Confirm whether you want Redwood-managed static egress or customer NAT (reply with public IPs if NAT).
- Confirm DoH vs native DNS for telemetry.
- Confirm acceptance of 30-min runbook review on 2026-10-12.

I'll also create a HubSpot ticket (HUBSPOT-234512) and upload the annotated SOC2 answers there.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
